SL-000008.transcript:
Member (Mei Lavoie): My dentist's claim came back declined and nobody's explained why.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Hi Mei Lavoie, Ryan MacDonald here — let me pull that up.
Member (Mei Lavoie): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Mei Lavoie): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Mei Lavoie): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Mei Lavoie): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?
Member (Mei Lavoie): The dentist sent it directly. That's how it's always worked before.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Has anything changed with your coverage, like a new job or a new dependant?
Member (Mei Lavoie): No, same job, same plan. My daughter was added last year but that's it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Did the dental office say anything about how they billed it?
Member (Mei Lavoie): They said they billed it the same way as always.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Let me take a look. I've compared this claim with the earlier paid claims on the file and the plan booklet.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Mei Lavoie): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): The earlier claims went through under a different benefit code. I've resubmitted this one under the right code, and it should be paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Mei Lavoie): So it was just the wrong code?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): That's what it looks like. I've resubmitted it under the basic services code, which matches what was done.
Member (Mei Lavoie): Do I need to tell my dentist?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): No need. I've added a note, and the payment will come to you since the claim was already paid at the office.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): So the claim has been resubmitted under the right code, and you should see it paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Mei Lavoie): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.
SL-000008.narrative_summary: Mei Lavoie, a Sun Life member, contacted support on a declined claim case. Agent Ryan MacDonald compared this claim with the earlier paid claims on the file and the plan booklet. In the end, it was resolved on this interaction, and the member rated it CSAT 5 (very satisfied).

Member (Emma Roy): My claim says paid, but the money isn't in my account.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Hi Emma Roy, Marc Tremblay here — let me pull that up.
Member (Emma Roy): I changed banks last month.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Let's find out where that payment went.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?

Agent (Marc Tremblay): How were you expecting to be paid?

Agent (Marc Tremblay): Did you get a payment notification in the app?

Agent (Marc Tremblay): Have any other claims come through since you switched?

Agent (Marc Tremblay): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): The payment was issued to the account on file on the 12th. I can open a trace, but it takes up to ten business days.
Member (Emma Roy): So I just wait again?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): I'm sorry, yes. The trace is open, and I've set a reminder to check it next week.
Member (Emma Roy): Can you call me when it's found?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): I've asked for a call-back once the trace is complete, and you'll also see it in the app.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): To recap: a payment trace is open, it can take up to ten business days, and you'll get a call when it's done.
Member (Emma Roy): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

SL-000083.transcript:
Member (Tyler Kim): My dentist's crown request under the Canadian Dental Care Plan was denied, and the letter doesn't say why.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Hi Tyler Kim, Daniel Okafor here — let me pull that up.
Member (Tyler Kim): The letter only says it doesn't meet plan criteria.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): I completely understand how frustrating that is — let me see what's actually happening on our end.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Can you confirm your CDCP member ID and date of birth?
Member (Tyler Kim): Yes, that's right.
Member (Tyler Kim): My dentist sent the X-rays twice.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Which procedure was the request for?
Member (Tyler Kim): A crown on a back tooth. My dentist says it's cracked.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Did the letter mention any documents that were missing?
Member (Tyler Kim): No, just that it doesn't meet the criteria.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Has the dental office called us about this directly?
Member (Tyler Kim): They said they called and got the same answer as me.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Are you in any pain right now?
Member (Tyler Kim): Some. It's manageable, but I can't chew on that side.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Let me take a look. I've reviewed the pre-authorization request and the documents received from the dental office.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): The assessment is done against the plan's criteria for crowns, which are set by Health Canada.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): I'm looking at the latest assessment on your file now.
Member (Tyler Kim): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): The decision follows the plan criteria set by Health Canada, and I don't have a more specific reason on my screen. Your dentist can submit a new request with more clinical notes, and I've noted that you asked for the reason.
Member (Tyler Kim): So nobody can tell me why?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): I know that's frustrating. I've asked for the specific criterion to be sent to you and your dentist in writing.
Member (Tyler Kim): What should my dentist include this time?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): A description of the crack, any symptoms, and a dated X-ray. Those are the most common gaps on crown requests.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): To recap: the denial stands for now, I've recorded your request for the specific reason, and your dentist can resubmit with more clinical notes.
Member (Tyler Kim): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.
SL-000083.narrative_summary: Tyler Kim, a Sun Life member, contacted support on a CDCP pre-authorization case. Agent Daniel Okafor reviewed the pre-authorization request and the documents received from the dental office. SL-000218.transcript:
Member (Noah Campbell): My medication claim was put on hold for more information and I don't know what you need.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Hi Noah Campbell, Ryan MacDonald here — let me pull that up.
Member (Noah Campbell): I uploaded the prescription through the app already.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Noah Campbell): Yes, that's right.
Member (Noah Campbell): My doctor charges 45 dollars to fill in forms.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Which medication or service is the request about?
Member (Noah Campbell): A new medication my specialist started me on last week.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Did the pharmacy give you the name of the form they need?
Member (Noah Campbell): They said 'prior authorization' and gave me a number to call. That's it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Is your doctor's office aware a form is needed?
Member (Noah Campbell): I told them, and they said they'd need the form itself from Sun Life.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): How much medication do you have left?
Member (Noah Campbell): About four days. That's why I'm calling now.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Let me take a look. I've checked the information request and the documents already on file.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Thanks for holding — I've got the full picture now.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): For this medication the plan needs a prior authorization from your doctor, not just the prescription.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I'm checking whether anything from your doctor's office is already on file.
Member (Noah Campbell): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): The drug is on the prior authorization list, so we need the completed form from your doctor before it can be covered. I've emailed you the form and noted that you're waiting on it.
Member (Noah Campbell): And I'm paying the doctor for the form on top of everything.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I understand. Keep the receipt for the form, and I'll note on your file how much medication you have left.
Member (Noah Campbell): How long does the review take once it's in?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Usually two to three business days. I've asked for it to be prioritised given your supply.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): To recap: the form is in your email, your doctor completes and faxes it, and the review usually takes two to three business days.
Member (Noah Campbell): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Arjun Campbell): I want to check whether my plan covers orthodontics for my son.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Hi Arjun Campbell, Priya Sandhu here — let me pull that up.
Member (Arjun Campbell): My spouse has coverage through her work too.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Good question to ask before you commit. Let me look.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Arjun Campbell): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Arjun Campbell): The orthodontist wants to start next month.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Do you have a treatment plan or cost estimate from the orthodontist?

Member (Arjun Campbell): No, this is the first time.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Is the orthodontist here in Canada?

Agent (Priya Sandhu): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Orthodontics isn't part of your employer's plan. I can send you the booklet section, and your plan administrator at work can confirm whether that's changing.
Member (Arjun Campbell): That's disappointing.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I understand. Some employers offer a health spending account that can be used for orthodontics.
Member (Arjun Campbell): How would I check that?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): It would show under Accounts in the app. I don't see one on your certificate, but HR can confirm.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): To recap: orthodontics isn't in your employer's plan right now, and HR can tell you if that's changing.
Member (Arjun Campbell): Alright, thank you for looking into it.

Member (Liam Singh): My dentist's claim came back declined and nobody's explained why.

Agent (Harpreet Gill): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Liam Singh): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?
Member (Liam Singh): The dentist sent it directly. That's how it's always worked before.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Has anything changed with your coverage, like a new job or a new dependant?
Member (Liam Singh): No, same job, same plan. My daughter was added last year but that's it.

Member (Liam Singh): They said they billed it the same way as always.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Let me take a look. I've compared this claim with the earlier paid claims on the file and the plan booklet.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Liam Singh): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): The earlier claims went through under a different benefit code. I've resubmitted this one under the right code, and it should be paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Liam Singh): So it was just the wrong code?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): That's what it looks like. I've resubmitted it under the basic services code, which matches what was done.
Member (Liam Singh): Do I need to tell my dentist?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): No need. I've added a note, and the payment will come to you since the claim was already paid at the office.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): To recap, everything's noted on your file, and the team will follow up with you.
Member (Liam Singh): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Noah Patel): My life insurance premium tripled and nobody warned me.

Member (Noah Patel): Alright, thank you for looking into it.

SL-000346.transcript:
Member (Chantal Wilson): I asked to transfer my pension from my old employer's plan to my bank and it still hasn't moved.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Hi Chantal Wilson, Kevin Nguyen here — let me pull that up.
Member (Chantal Wilson): The receiving institution says they never got anything.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): I completely understand how frustrating that is — let me see what's actually happening on our end.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Chantal Wilson): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Chantal Wilson): The market's moved since then and I've lost money waiting.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Where is the money going?
Member (Chantal Wilson): To an RRSP at my bank. They say they're waiting on Sun Life.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): When did you send in the transfer request?
Member (Chantal Wilson): In June. I signed everything they sent me.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Have you received any statement showing the transfer as pending?
Member (Chantal Wilson): Only the annual statement, which still shows the balance with you.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Let me take a look. I've traced the transfer request and the paperwork on the plan account.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Your request came in on June 14. The transfer is waiting on the signed transfer authorization from the receiving institution, which is standard for locked-in pension money.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Until that form arrives, the funds stay invested in your current options, so they've moved with the market.
Member (Chantal Wilson): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Member (Chantal Wilson): So is this actually getting fixed today?
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): The transfer is waiting on the signed transfer form from the receiving institution. I can't release it until that arrives, but I've sent them a reminder.
Member (Chantal Wilson): So I've lost money because of a form nobody told me about?
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): I understand. I've noted on your file that you've been waiting since June, so it's visible if this needs a review.
Member (Chantal Wilson): Who follows up?
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Retirement services will. I've asked them to call you once the form arrives.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): To recap: we're waiting on your bank's signed form, a reminder has gone to them today, and retirement services will call you when it's in.
Member (Chantal Wilson): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Thanks for bearing with me. Everything's noted on your file, and you'll hear back as I said.

Member (Liam Ahmed): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): The earlier claims went through under a different benefit code. I've resubmitted this one under the right code, and it should be paid at 80% within five business days.

Agent (Harpreet Gill): That's what it looks like. I've resubmitted it under the basic services code, which matches what was done.
Member (Liam Ahmed): Do I need to tell my dentist?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): No need. I've added a note, and the payment will come to you since the claim was already paid at the office.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): So the claim has been resubmitted under the right code, and you should see it paid at 80% within five business days.

Member (Mei Cote): My dentist's crown request under the Canadian Dental Care Plan was denied, and the letter doesn't say why.

Agent (Ryan MacDonald): The first request was missing the radiograph date. The second one is complete and has been assessed, and it's approved. Your dentist will get the confirmation today.

Agent (Ryan MacDonald): That depends on your co-payment level. Your dentist will see it on the confirmation.

Member (Noah Chen): My dentist's claim came back declined and nobody's explained why.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Hi Noah Chen, Harpreet Gill here — let me pull that up.
Member (Noah Chen): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): I completely understand how frustrating that is — let me see what's actually happening on our end.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Noah Chen): Yes, that's right.
Member (Noah Chen): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Noah Chen): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?
Member (Noah Chen): The dentist sent it directly. That's how it's always worked before.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Has this type of claim been paid before?
Member (Noah Chen): Yes, in the spring. Same dentist, same kind of work, and it went through with no problem.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Has anything changed with your coverage, like a new job or a new dependant?
Member (Noah Chen): No, same job, same plan. My daughter was added last year but that's it.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Let me take a look. I've compared this claim with the earlier paid claims on the file and the plan booklet.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Noah Chen): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): The earlier claims went through under a different benefit code. I've resubmitted this one under the right code, and it should be paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Noah Chen): So it was just the wrong code?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): That's what it looks like. I've resubmitted it under the basic services code, which matches what was done.
Member (Noah Chen): Do I need to tell my dentist?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): No need. I've added a note, and the payment will come to you since the claim was already paid at the office.

Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Hi Arjun Chen, Chloe Gagnon here — let me pull that up.
Member (Arjun Chen): My doctor charges 45 dollars to fill in forms.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Arjun Chen): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Arjun Chen): I uploaded the prescription through the app already.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Which medication or service is the request about?
Member (Arjun Chen): A new medication my specialist started me on last week.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Which pharmacy are you using?
Member (Arjun Chen): The one near my work. They said they can resubmit as soon as it's approved.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Is your doctor's office aware a form is needed?
Member (Arjun Chen): I told them, and they said they'd need the form itself from Sun Life.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): How much medication do you have left?
Member (Arjun Chen): About four days. That's why I'm calling now.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Let me take a look. I've checked the information request and the documents already on file.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): For this medication the plan needs a prior authorization from your doctor, not just the prescription.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): I'm checking whether anything from your doctor's office is already on file.
Member (Arjun Chen): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): The prior authorization form is on file from last week. It just wasn't linked to the drug claim. I've linked it, and the pharmacy can resubmit today.
Member (Arjun Chen): So I can pick it up today?
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Yes. The authorization is linked to the claim now, so the pharmacy can resubmit and it should go through.
Member (Arjun Chen): Will I have to do this every time?
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): No. It's approved for twelve months, so refills go through automatically.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): So you're all set: the authorization is on file for twelve months and the pharmacy can process it today.
Member (Arjun Chen): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Mathieu Kim): I've been off work for six weeks and still haven't had a decision on my short-term disability claim.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Hi Mathieu Kim, Priya Sandhu here — let me pull that up.
Member (Mathieu Kim): My employer says they sent their part weeks ago.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I completely understand how frustrating that is — let me see what's actually happening on our end.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?

Member (Mathieu Kim): I don't know who my case manager is.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Do you know roughly when HR sent their statement?
Member (Mathieu Kim): They said about three weeks ago, but I haven't seen anything confirming it.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Have you been contacted by a case manager yet?
Member (Mathieu Kim): Not that I know of. Nobody has called me.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Is there a good number and time to reach you?
Member (Mathieu Kim): My mobile, any time before three. I have appointments in the afternoons.

Agent (Priya Sandhu): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Your file has your statement and your doctor's statement. I'm checking whether the employer's statement has come in.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Once the file is complete, the case manager makes the decision and calls you to explain it.
Member (Mathieu Kim): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Your claim was approved yesterday. The first payment goes out Friday, and your case manager will call you this week to talk about your return-to-work plan.
Member (Mathieu Kim): So when does the first payment come?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): It's scheduled for Friday, and it includes the weeks since your waiting period ended.
Member (Mathieu Kim): Who do I contact if something changes?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Your case manager is Denise. I've sent you her direct line by secure message.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): To recap, everything's noted on your file, and the team will follow up with you.
Member (Mathieu Kim): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Olivia Campbell): The chat assistant told me to call. I've been on hold for over an hour.

Agent (Jasmine Wong): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Olivia Campbell): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Olivia Campbell): I just want to submit a claim for my son's glasses.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Did you get any email from us about the lock?
Member (Olivia Campbell): No, nothing.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): When did you last log in successfully?
Member (Olivia Campbell): A couple of months ago. I've tried resetting the password three times this week.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Did the chat give you a reference number?

Agent (Jasmine Wong): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Online claim submission is only available during certain hours for that benefit, so I can't submit it for you tonight. You can submit it in the app from 6 a.m. Eastern tomorrow.
Member (Olivia Campbell): So I have to call back tomorrow?
Agent (Jasmine Wong): You don't need to call. You can submit in the app from 6 a.m. Eastern, and I've unlocked the account so it'll work.
Member (Olivia Campbell): And if it locks again?
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Use the 'forgot password' link only once, then wait 30 minutes. I've added a note in case you need to call.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): To recap: your account is unlocked, the claim can go in from 6 a.m. Eastern, and there's a note on your file if anything goes wrong.
Member (Olivia Campbell): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Chantal Cote): My son needs braces and I want to know what my plan pays before we commit.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Hi Chantal Cote, Daniel Okafor here — let me pull that up.
Member (Chantal Cote): My spouse has coverage through her work too.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Happy to check that for you.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Chantal Cote): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Chantal Cote): The orthodontist wants to start next month.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Is he listed as a dependant on your plan?
Member (Chantal Cote): Yes, since he was born.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Do you have a treatment plan or cost estimate from the orthodontist?

Agent (Daniel Okafor): Has he had any orthodontic work covered before?

Agent (Daniel Okafor): If your spouse has coverage too, their plan can pick up part of what's left after ours pays.

Agent (Daniel Okafor): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Orthodontics is covered at 50% up to a 2,500-dollar lifetime maximum for dependants under 19. I recommend a pre-determination first, and I've emailed you the steps.
Member (Chantal Cote): What's a pre-determination?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): The orthodontist sends the treatment plan first, and we confirm exactly what's covered before any work starts.
Member (Chantal Cote): Great, that helps.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): I'll also send the coordination-of-benefits form for your spouse's plan.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): So, 50% up to 2,500 dollars, a pre-determination first, and your spouse's plan can cover part of the rest.
Member (Chantal Cote): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Mei Patel): My dentist's claim came back declined and nobody's explained why.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Hi Mei Patel, Ryan MacDonald here — let me pull that up.
Member (Mei Patel): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Mei Patel): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Mei Patel): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Mei Patel): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?
Member (Mei Patel): The dentist sent it directly. That's how it's always worked before.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Has this type of claim been paid before?
Member (Mei Patel): Yes, in the spring. Same dentist, same kind of work, and it went through with no problem.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Did the dental office say anything about how they billed it?
Member (Mei Patel): They said they billed it the same way as always.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Let me take a look. I've compared this claim with the earlier paid claims on the file and the plan booklet.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Thanks for holding — I've got the full picture now.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Mei Patel): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Member (Mei Patel): So is this actually getting fixed today?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): The decline is correct under your employer's plan, because this service has an annual maximum and it's been reached. I can send you the plan wording, and your plan administrator at work can confirm the limits.
Member (Mei Patel): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Mei Patel): Can I appeal it?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): You can ask for a review. I've opened one and noted that you weren't told about the separate maximum.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Mei Patel): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Thanks for bearing with me. Everything's noted on your file, and you'll hear back as I said.

Member (Tyler Martin): My pension transfer has been sitting for months and my bank says they're waiting on you.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Hi Tyler Martin, Ryan MacDonald here — let me pull that up.
Member (Tyler Martin): The receiving institution says they never got anything.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I completely understand how frustrating that is — let me see what's actually happening on our end.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Tyler Martin): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Tyler Martin): The market's moved since then and I've lost money waiting.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Which plan is the transfer from?
Member (Tyler Martin): My old employer's pension plan. I left the company in May.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Where is the money going?
Member (Tyler Martin): To an RRSP at my bank. They say they're waiting on Sun Life.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Did the bank send you a transfer form to sign as well?
Member (Tyler Martin): I think so. They handled their side.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Have you received any statement showing the transfer as pending?
Member (Tyler Martin): Only the annual statement, which still shows the balance with you.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Let me take a look. I've traced the transfer request and the paperwork on the plan account.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Thanks for holding — I've got the full picture now.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Your request came in on June 14. The transfer is waiting on the signed transfer authorization from the receiving institution, which is standard for locked-in pension money.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Until that form arrives, the funds stay invested in your current options, so they've moved with the market.
Member (Tyler Martin): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): The transfer is waiting on the signed transfer form from the receiving institution. I can't release it until that arrives, but I've sent them a reminder.
Member (Tyler Martin): So I've lost money because of a form nobody told me about?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I understand. I've noted on your file that you've been waiting since June, so it's visible if this needs a review.
Member (Tyler Martin): Who follows up?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Retirement services will. I've asked them to call you once the form arrives.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): To recap: we're waiting on your bank's signed form, a reminder has gone to them today, and retirement services will call you when it's in.
Member (Tyler Martin): That's not really the answer I was hoping for, but okay.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I've logged everything here so if this comes up again, the next agent has the full picture.

Member (Mei Lavoie): My medication claim was put on hold for more information and I don't know what you need.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Hi Mei Lavoie, Priya Sandhu here — let me pull that up.
Member (Mei Lavoie): I uploaded the prescription through the app already.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Mei Lavoie): Yes, that's right.
Member (Mei Lavoie): My doctor charges 45 dollars to fill in forms.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Which medication or service is the request about?
Member (Mei Lavoie): A new medication my specialist started me on last week.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Did the pharmacy give you the name of the form they need?
Member (Mei Lavoie): They said 'prior authorization' and gave me a number to call. That's it.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Is your doctor's office aware a form is needed?
Member (Mei Lavoie): I told them, and they said they'd need the form itself from Sun Life.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): How much medication do you have left?
Member (Mei Lavoie): About four days. That's why I'm calling now.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Let me take a look. I've checked the information request and the documents already on file.

Agent (Priya Sandhu): I'm checking whether anything from your doctor's office is already on file.

Agent (Priya Sandhu): The drug is on the prior authorization list, so we need the completed form from your doctor before it can be covered. I've emailed you the form and noted that you're waiting on it.
Member (Mei Lavoie): And I'm paying the doctor for the form on top of everything.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I understand. Keep the receipt for the form, and I'll note on your file how much medication you have left.
Member (Mei Lavoie): How long does the review take once it's in?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Usually two to three business days. I've asked for it to be prioritised given your supply.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): To recap: the form is in your email, your doctor completes and faxes it, and the review usually takes two to three business days.
Member (Mei Lavoie): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Leila Wilson): My pension transfer has been sitting for months and my bank says they're waiting on you.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Hi Leila Wilson, Daniel Okafor here — let me pull that up.

Agent (Daniel Okafor): Yes. The form arrived this morning, and I've released the transfer.
Member (Leila Wilson): How long until my bank has it?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Usually five business days, and you'll get a confirmation letter from us.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): So the transfer is released and should reach your bank within five business days.
Member (Leila Wilson): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

SL-002029.transcript:
Member (Leila Roy): My dental claim was declined, and the same kind of claim was paid in the spring.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Hi Leila Roy, Ryan MacDonald here — let me pull that up.
Member (Leila Roy): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Leila Roy): Yes, that's right.
Member (Leila Roy): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Leila Roy): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?
Member (Leila Roy): The dentist sent it directly. That's how it's always worked before.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Has this type of claim been paid before?
Member (Leila Roy): Yes, in the spring. Same dentist, same kind of work, and it went through with no problem.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Has anything changed with your coverage, like a new job or a new dependant?
Member (Leila Roy): No, same job, same plan. My daughter was added last year but that's it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Let me take a look. I've compared this claim with the earlier paid claims on the file and the plan booklet.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Leila Roy): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Member (Leila Roy): So is this actually getting fixed today?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): The decline is correct under your employer's plan, because this service has an annual maximum and it's been reached. I can send you the plan wording, and your plan administrator at work can confirm the limits.
Member (Leila Roy): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Leila Roy): Can I appeal it?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): You can ask for a review. I've opened one and noted that you weren't told about the separate maximum.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Leila Roy): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Thanks for bearing with me. Everything's noted on your file, and you'll hear back as I said.

Member (Tyler Cote): My son needs braces and I want to know what my plan pays before we commit.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Hi Tyler Cote, Chloe Gagnon here — let me pull that up.
Member (Tyler Cote): My spouse has coverage through her work too.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Good question to ask before you commit. Let me look.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Tyler Cote): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Tyler Cote): The orthodontist wants to start next month.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Is he listed as a dependant on your plan?
Member (Tyler Cote): Yes, since he was born.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): How old is he?
Member (Tyler Cote): Fourteen.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Has he had any orthodontic work covered before?

Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Orthodontic coverage depends on your employer's plan, so I'm checking your certificate now.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): If your spouse has coverage too, their plan can pick up part of what's left after ours pays.
Member (Tyler Cote): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Orthodontics is covered at 50% up to a 2,500-dollar lifetime maximum for dependants under 19. I recommend a pre-determination first, and I've emailed you the steps.
Member (Tyler Cote): What's a pre-determination?
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): The orthodontist sends the treatment plan first, and we confirm exactly what's covered before any work starts.
Member (Tyler Cote): Great, that helps.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): I'll also send the coordination-of-benefits form for your spouse's plan.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): So, 50% up to 2,500 dollars, a pre-determination first, and your spouse's plan can cover part of the rest.
Member (Tyler Cote): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Mei Roy): Yes, that's right.
Member (Mei Roy): I just want to submit a claim for my son's glasses.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): When did you last log in successfully?
Member (Mei Roy): A couple of months ago. I've tried resetting the password three times this week.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Did you try the chat assistant?
Member (Mei Roy): Yes, Ella told me to call. Then I waited over an hour on hold.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Are you on the app or the website right now?
Member (Mei Roy): The app on my phone.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Let me take a look. I've checked the account's login status and the claim submission history.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Thanks for holding — I've got the full picture now.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): The account locked after several reset attempts in a row. That's a security setting, not something you did wrong.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Once it's unlocked, you'll set a new password and it'll stay unlocked.
Member (Mei Roy): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Online claim submission is only available during certain hours for that benefit, so I can't submit it for you tonight. You can submit it in the app from 6 a.m. Eastern tomorrow.
Member (Mei Roy): So I have to call back tomorrow?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): You don't need to call. You can submit in the app from 6 a.m. Eastern, and I've unlocked the account so it'll work.
Member (Mei Roy): And if it locks again?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Use the 'forgot password' link only once, then wait 30 minutes. I've added a note in case you need to call.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): To recap: your account is unlocked, the claim can go in from 6 a.m. Eastern, and there's a note on your file if anything goes wrong.
Member (Mei Roy): That's not really the answer I was hoping for, but okay.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I've logged everything here so if this comes up again, the next agent has the full picture.
